message.reasoning:
I'm decoding the garbled text and piecing together the request: an HTML animation of someone biking along a seaside road, with the main character required to be a specific bird—likely a pelican, given the description of a large white water bird with an orange-yellow beak and a throat pouch.

This needs to be a single self-contained HTML file with inline CSS and JS, no external resources, featuring continuous animation like pedaling or rotating wheels, plus coastal scenery like sea, sky, and road. I'm planning to build this with canvas-based animation: a rotating crank and inverse-kinematic legs for pedaling, spinning wheels with spokes, and a parallax background with sky gradient, sun, clouds, waves, islands, and a dashed road with guardrails and palm trees, while designing the pelican itself with its characteristic bill, pouch, folded neck, wings resting on the handlebars, and webbed orange feet on the pedals.

Working out the precise coordinates for the bike frame now -- wheel centers, bottom bracket, seat, head tube, handlebar stem, and crank/pedal positions -- along with where the pelican's hip attaches to the seat.

That range works, with wheel radius 50 centered appropriately. Now I'm laying out the bike frame tubes, fork, and handlebar coordinates, then sketching the pelican's tilted body ellipse, tail, and neck curving up into the head position.

Adding the bill, pouch, eye, and crest, plus a folded wing shaped to extend forward like an arm reaching the handlebar grip, with tapered dark primary feathers. Now I'm working out the leg placement using inverse kinematics so the orange webbed feet land properly on the pedals, planning to draw the far leg and pedal first so they sit behind the bike structure.

For the IK math, I'm computing the knee angle from hip-to-pedal distance and leg segment lengths so the knee bends forward naturally in canvas coordinates. I'll also add a subtle body bob synced to the pedaling motion for a lively feel.

Now I'm laying out the whole scene with parallax speeds: clouds and islands drift slowest, sea has gentle waves, and palm trees/guardrails scroll fast matching road speed. I'm stacking layers from sky gradient down through clouds, distant islands, sparkling sea with wave lines, sandy beach, and a gray dashed road where the bike rides at a fixed height, with guardrail posts and simple v-shaped birds overhead rounding out the composition.

Writing canvas setup...

I want road scroll speed tied to wheel rotation for visual consistency, with wheel angle derived from distance and wheel radius. For the foreground I'll place palm trees on the beach strip behind the road at a slightly offset speed for depth, then set up the bike drawing function with its own coordinate translation and scaling.

Now I'm sketching the wheel rendering with tire, rim, spokes, and hub, plus the frame color, chainring, chain lines, crank arms, and pedal rectangle. For the pelican's leg, I'm positioning the ankle relative to the pedal point and starting the webbed foot shape as a simple triangle.

Still working out the foot polygon...

I'm layering the pelican's body: a tail fan, a shaded white body ellipse, folded wing with dark trailing primaries, and a feathered wing-arm reaching toward the handlebar grip, now starting the neck curve from the shoulder point.

Continuing the head and bill shapes with the hooked upper mandible and sagging throat pouch...

Now I'm working out the draw order and layering: far leg and crank behind the frame, near leg and crank in front, with the neck, head, bill, and wing drawn last so the wing hand covers the handlebar grip. I'm also adding a subtle shadow ellipse beneath the bike and considering a slight body bob synced to the pedal crank for liveliness.

I'm skipping extra speed lines but thinking about a minimal caption in the title tag instead of on-canvas text. Now I'm setting up the sky and wave rendering, with waves spaced progressively toward shore and drifting arcs for motion, plus initializing a handful of clouds with randomized positions.

Writing cloud, island, and road parallax...

Writing wheel and chain drawing logic...

Adding more frame details...

Thigh color white-ish, shin orange with a knee joint circle; far leg uses darker shades for depth. For crank positions I'm computing pedal locations from the bottom bracket using the crank angle, and setting wheel rotation so motion direction matches clockwise spin when moving right.

Still drawing the pelican: head bob tied to crank cycle, near wing as a filled path with feather tips in black, and a folded wing shape layered over the body with darker primary feathers extending past the tail.

Now I'm shaping the neck with a curved stroke into the head position, giving it a pale yellow crown, then building the bill as a hooked upper mandible curving outward from the face.

I'm layering a semi-transparent pouch beneath the mandible that wobbles with the bird's bob motion, adding a pink-skinned eye, and shifting all upper body parts by the bob offset while keeping the hip anchored for leg stability.

Now I'm adding scene details: a soft shadow under the bike, sun shimmer on the sea, foaming shoreline waves, and a guardrail with posts matching road speed, plus palm trees on the sand moving at a slightly slower parallax rate. Finally I'll assemble the complete code and make sure to clamp delta time when the tab is hidden.
